items.text: A lot of content on this topic oversells the skill-first shift.
Each has a distinct proof format, entry cost, and honest ceiling.
Do not build a single-tool profile.
These six lanes were chosen because each one has real, current hiring demand in India for people without a degree, not because they sound exciting on a listicle.
Commission-heavy pay with almost no formal entry barrier.
A real but slower route now: 6-12 months from bootcamp finish to hire, and only for people who ship deployed projects, not just certificates.

blocks.heading: Four Questions Before You Pick a Lane

items.text: Six lanes is still a lot to choose between.
Do you get energy from talking to strangers all day, or does that drain you fast.
How much runway, money, and time do you actually have right now.

blocks.heading: Mistakes That Waste the Head Start

items.text: A stack of unfinished course certificates looks weaker than one real, finished project you can explain in detail.
Sending a no-degree resume into a large corporate's campus-only pipeline is a mismatch, not a rejection of your skill.
The certificate gets you past the first screen at best.

figures.label: Pay Range

visuals.heading: Not Just Old-Fashioned Worry

items.text: Applicant tracking systems at large corporates auto-filter resumes on a degree field before a human ever sees them.
Campus placement drives, by definition, only reach people enrolled in a degree program.
Government and public-sector jobs almost always list a specific degree as a hard eligibility line, not a preference.
Family and social pressure treats "no degree" as a red flag long before an employer ever gets the chance to judge your actual skill.

blocks.heading: Proof of Work Replaces the Missing Degree

items.text: Some baseline competence, verified by a third party.
Persistence over a fixed multi-year period.
A recognisable brand an HR filter already trusts.
Eligibility for roles that legally require it.
